tools_used: pypdf (local text extraction of fetched PDFs)
helpful: The sal-v4 segment base-rate table with bracketed reached rates gave a clean anchor for the frozen band.
CourtListener read_document returned the full D.C. Circuit opinion in three chunks, which settled the panel, the holding, and what the petitioner conceded below.
supremecourt.gov docket pages for the linked stay application were the single most informative retrieval: the stay denial order and the respondent's text-extractable opposition previewed the BIO.
gaps: No OCR path: the petition, the redacted application, and the reply are image-only scans, so the questions presented were unavailable from any first-party source. An OCR fallback in document provisioning (or in the cell) would have closed this.
fedcourts query has no subject filter usable here (--topic is circuit-only), so corpus priors could not be narrowed to reporter's-privilege or contempt cases; the returned priors were unrelated.

The distribution parser counted a linked motion's distribution as the petition's; a per-entry attribution (petition vs. linked motion) in context.json would avoid an off-by-one in relist-increment baselines.

Linked-docket provisioning: the snapshot's Links field names 26M17 and the case has a prior stay docket (25A1448); provisioning those dockets' entries alongside the petition's would have saved several web fetches.
notes: Two news fetches hit a paywall (HTTP 402 after redirect); the underlying facts were recovered from the Court's own docket pages instead.
